title: Nexus
description: An all-in-one enterprise collaboration workspace — team chat, work calendar, video meetings, tasks, tickets and AI-generated meeting recaps — serving 30,000+ active users.
about: Nexus is a B2B SaaS collaboration workspace: think Slack, Google Calendar, Zoom and Asana combined into one enterprise tool, with AI meeting recaps on top. The frontend is a Module Federation micro-frontend estate of 6+ independently deployable modules, with offline-first data access and socket-based real-time synchronisation across web and Electron desktop clients.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented real-time features using WebSockets
Led frontend architecture for web and Electron-based desktop applications
Owned the frontend architecture for the rebuild of the collaboration suite serving 30,000+ active users
Split the product into a Module Federation micro-frontend estate of 6+ independently deployable modules
Built offline-first data access with Zustand, TanStack Query and IndexedDB
Designed a deep-linking system spanning 6 modules (Calendar, Task, Chat, Home, Recap, Drive)
Introduced the company's first Playwright end-to-end suite and held unit coverage above 60% with Jest and React Testing Library
Built the AI meeting-recap experience, a post-meeting summary page distributed to attendees by link
Set frontend standards and code-review practice adopted across the company's ~15 frontend engineers

title: Alkafeel ERP Ecosystem
description: A modular ERP covering HR and administrative workflows, built as a Vue.js micro-frontend estate deployed independently by 5+ teams.
about: An enterprise ERP ecosystem for HR and administrative operations, built with Vue.js and Module Federation so that each team ships its own modules without a coordinated release. The work replaced email approval chains and manual data re-entry with in-app submission, automated approval routing and real-time SignalR notifications.
responsibilities: Developed a Vue.js Module Federation architecture enabling independent deployments for 5+ teams, eliminating cross-team release dependencies and system-wide downtime
Automated HR and administrative request workflows, replacing email chains and manual data re-entry with in-app submission and automated approval routing
Delivered real-time SignalR notifications for approvals and company-wide announcements
Built 50+ admin and back-office screens covering request forms, approval queues, permission-aware data tables and role-based views
Implemented RTL-first layouts for Arabic users and maintained UI consistency across distributed deployments

title: LandLogic
description: A geospatial web platform used by Canadian municipalities for land-use planning and permit issuance.
about: A map-based planning system handling large-scale geospatial data and dynamic reporting. The frontend renders 10,000+ simultaneous map layers in Mapbox GL JS — replacing a viewer that stalled past a few hundred — and assembles planning documents of 150+ pages from live data feeds.
responsibilities: Rendered 10,000+ simultaneous map layers in Mapbox GL JS with custom performance optimizations, replacing a viewer that stalled past a few hundred
Built a data-driven reporting engine generating 150+ page geospatial reports from live data feeds
Developed parcel-based dynamic reporting pages
Optimized rendering and state management for large datasets
Collaborated with cross-functional teams in an Agile environment
